subject: Contract extension & region plan: EU primary, APAC standby
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@aurorahealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-20T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Contract extension + EU primary request

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the conversation yesterday. Aurora Health Systems is preparing to extend our current agreement (expires 2026-12-01) and we want to make two platform changes in the next term:

- Make EU hosting the primary residency for PHI and PII (we will continue to send US traffic but storage/processing of patient records must reside in EU).
- Add an APAC standby region for failover and predictable burst capacity (we anticipate peak traffic during APAC business hours and want warm standby for failover).

High-level asks: updated SOW + pricing for reserved EU capacity (baseline + 2x peak burst), APAC standby licensing (billed as reserved standby), and a quarterly failover test plan. Also need confirmation on data residency controls and evidence (DPA + any SOC2 artifacts).

Can Redwood put a proposed amendment and MOP (runbook) together so we can review with procurement/legal? We’re targeting sign-off by end of November to meet provisioning timelines.

Appreciate it —
Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Platform Engineering
Aurora Health Systems
From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-20T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Contract extension + EU primary request

Samir — thanks for the clear list. We can support EU as primary residency and provide an APAC warm-standby failover model.

Immediate next steps I recommend:
1) I’ll circulate a draft amendment (SOW + billing table) that converts your current reserved pool to an EU-primary sku and adds an APAC standby sku.
2) Marissa and Ben — can you review pricing and SLA implications? We should call out the uplift for reserved standby capacity and the SLA during failover windows.
3) Samir / procurement — share any procurement constraints (PO terms, signature workflow).

We can do a short sync next week (30 min) to walk the amendment. If sign-off by 11/22 is feasible, we can schedule infra provisioning to meet your target.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-22T08:35:00-07:00
Subject: RE: pricing + DPA implications for Aurora amendment

Folks —

Quick notes from pricing/legal perspective:
- Pricing: propose baseline reserved EU capacity (committed vCPUs/GPU hours) + a standby APAC SKU billed at 20% of baseline (reserved standby pricing) to hold capacity and enable <1s warm failover. Burst above standby would be billed at on-demand token rates.
- SLA: standard SLA remains; during a planned failover test window we’ll provide a temporary elevated support cell. Unplanned failover will fall back to a 99.5% latency SLO for the first 24 hours while caches rehydrate.
- DPA/Data residency: need an amendment to the DPA specifying EU data as primary; add an annex referencing the EU data processing locations and encryption-at-rest keys scope. Ops will need a signed DPA before provisioning.

I’m attaching a short excerpt from the geo-failover runbook (capacity_runbook_excerpt.txt) that we can include in the SOW appendix.

Attachments: capacity_runbook_excerpt.txt

-Marissa
VP, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@aurorahealth.com>, Ava Li <ava.li@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-27T10:20:00-07:00
Subject: Proposed amendment + scheduling: Aurora Health Systems (AUR-2026-EXT1)

Samir / Ava —

Attached is the draft amendment (aurora_amendment_v1.pdf) that covers:
- Term extension to 2027-12-01
- EU primary residency clause and DPA annex language
- APAC standby reserved capacity line item (20% uplift as Marissa described)
- Failover testing cadence (quarterly) + runbook excerpt included
- Pricing table and provisioning lead times (EU reserved capacity: 6 weeks; APAC standby: 4 weeks to bring to warm state)

HubSpot link with deal details: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/company/aurora-health-systems
DocuSign for amendment when ready: https://www.docusign.net/prepare/ABC-aurora-amendment

If you’re comfortable we’ll route to signature. One operational note: provisioning EU-primary capacity requires a signed DPA + confirmation of encryption key custody (we can support KMS integration).

Propose a 30-minute call Thursday 10/29 to walk the amendment and highlight provisioning windows.

Thanks —
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
Attachment: aurora_amendment_v1.pdf
From: Ava Li <ava.li@aurorahealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: procurement@aurorahealth.com
Date: 2026-11-05T13:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed amendment + scheduling: Aurora Health Systems (AUR-2026-EXT1)

Karthik — thanks for the draft. A couple items procurement/legal flagged before we can sign:
1) We need a 60-day notice requirement documented for any planned cutover that would affect production traffic for EU-primary migration.
2) Please provide SOC 2 evidence and the latest pen-test report — these are required for our security board.
3) For the failover tests, we require a runbook and a dry-run schedule at least two weeks prior to the test window.

Samir and I will aim to review the amendment this week. Assuming approvals, procurement will need a final PDF for PO processing and we’ll route via DocuSign.

—Ava
Ava Li
Senior Procurement Manager
Aurora Health Systems

Subject: Final steps: amendment, evidence and provisioning windows

Ava / Samir —

Thanks for the review call earlier. Per procurement items:
- We added a 60-day planned-cutover notice clause to section 3.4 of the amendment.
- SOC 2 report and pen-test summary are uploaded here: https://drive.redwood.ai/runbooks/geo-failover-aurora-2026 (bottom of the folder).
- Attached is the runbook excerpt (capacity_runbook_excerpt.txt) showing the dry-run checklist and required notifications. We’ll publish the full runbook in the shared drive once amendment is signed.

Requested timeline: if Aurora can sign the DocuSign by 2026-11-22, we can begin EU provisioning the week of 2026-12-07 and have a warm APAC standby ready by 2027-01-15. Quarterly failover test windows will be scheduled with two-week advance notices.
